best_signals: RSI 55-60 at entry: 2/2 wins (100%), avg +2.15% -- the ONLY consistently profitable bucket for the LEGACY intraday RSI strategy; n=2, thin sample, INFORMATIONAL ONLY now that the live strategy is MA-20/60 trend-following. Do not act on it without n>=10.

Single shallow-cross probation entries (heavy size-DOWN, NOT skip) -- verdict POSITIVE and durable. BMY (0.13% cross, 50% unit) remains the book's premier anchor at +14.29% Day 42 (gave back a hair from +15.47%). GIS (0.29% cross, 75% unit) ~flat at +12.67% Day 44. CAG (0.113% cross, 50% unit) firmed to +6.97% Day 31. MOS (0.43% matured cross, 75% unit) ~flat at +0.32% Day 3. Read: the discipline keeps validating; size down on a single clean shallow cross, do not upsize, weight the entry's SECTOR trend.

Idiosyncratic single-name upside is real and can dominate a day (CRM +23% Aug 27) -- the mirror image of the single-name downside risk (AMZN/DVN). It does NOT reflect a strategy edge and is not repeatable on demand; treat record days built on one name's pop as luck-of-the-draw, not proof the tilt beats up tapes. The lasting lesson is symmetric: MA-20/60 trend entries carry fat single-name tails in BOTH directions, which is exactly why size discipline (size-down on flags) and fixed 2xATR stops matter.

Defensive/quality tilt -- reads STRUCTURAL and tape-conditional. The edge has paid on every down tape (Tue Aug 18 +1.31pt, Thu Aug 20 +0.81pt, Mon Aug 24 +0.84pt) and stayed roughly even-to-negative on up tapes (Wed Aug 20 +0.95pt was the exception; Fri +0.04pt, Tue Aug 25 -0.54pt, Wed Aug 26 -0.06pt). Today's +1.83pt on a STRONG up tape looks like a counterexample but is not -- it is a CRM single-name pop, not the tilt; ex-CRM the book was flat-to-behind, fitting the read exactly. Expect the tilt's own beat to reappear on the next down/flat tape. The Aug 17 limit still stands (the tilt does NOT immunize against an idiosyncratic single-name stop-out like AMZN, or a single-name fade like DVN).
avoid: Extended entries (price well above EMA-20 at entry) -- CONFIRMED LOSER, thesis RESOLVED by AMZN (entered Aug 4 at +15.2% above EMA20, stopped out Aug 17 at -6.57%, -$619.82; prior confirm META Jul 15 ~8.5% ext, stopped -8.04% Jul 23). CRM (Aug 4, +7.2% ext) is the standout exception at +36.1% after today's pop, cushion ~33%. Firm rule stands: treat >~6-8% above-EMA extension as size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback; when it co-occurs with a shallow cross, SKIP outright.

STACKED-FLAG entries (shallow cross + extended above EMA + thin liquidity together) -- RESOLVED as a SKIP, not a size-down: PDBC (0.15% cross + ~6.05% extended + thin liq, quarter-unit Jul 24) stopped out -2.40% Day 3. Distinguish from a SINGLE shallow-cross flag (BMY/GIS/CAG/MOS), a valid size-DOWN. Rule: one flag -> size down; two or more stacked -> skip. CRM (Aug 4) carried TWO soft flags (0.34% cross + 7.2% ext) but no thin-liq strike; now +36.1% Day 23 after a single-name pop, so the two-soft-flag boundary test reads clearly POSITIVE. DVN (Aug 18) two-soft-flag test (0.162% cross + ~6.8% ext, no thin-liq strike; turtle unit) firmed to -2.20% Day 8 (from -2.71%) but remains the weakest two-soft-flag case and an idiosyncratic single-name soft spot; still not a realized loser, watch closely. PSKY (Aug 24) two-soft-flag test (0.503% confirmed cross + 6.27% ext, thin liquidity but not a hard thin-liq STRIKE) at +4.91% Day 4 -- reads positive so far. Keep the one-flag-size-down / two-flag-skip rule as is.

Shallow EMA cross entries on earnings-adjacent names: TSLA (Jul 7, 0.06% cross, earnings Jul 22) lost -4.78%. Rule: SKIP (do not size down) when BOTH shallow cross (<0.5%) AND earnings within 14 days.
